notes: This software archive is the public PicoTorch source tree. Training remains on PC PyTorch. Raw WISDM and CIFAR-10 archives, PlatformIO .pio trees, and ESP-IDF managed_components are not redistributed. Pico-Former is an independently developed glucose application, archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22218446. The host protocol is archived as RICE-Former, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22171786.
description:
This software archive provides PicoTorch, an open source deep learning framework on ESP32 that accelerates the path from research prototyping to on-device deployment. Built to be flexible and modular, it assembles a Module graph and runs one forward.

The repository supports independent audit of four connected designs: (1) a Module graph assembled from Linear, LayerNorm, multi-head attention, feed-forward, and Sequential, run as one forward; (2) fused self-attention and cross-attention implemented in this library in hardware FP32 on ESP32-S3; (3) a same-precision contrast with LiteRT Micro FP32 on one WISDM weight set; and (4) the Espressif INT8 official path listed as a separate precision tier. PicoTorch does not call ESP-DL, ESP-NN, or ESP-PPQ. Training stays on PC PyTorch.

Included materials

  • Public C++ headers and kernels (include/picotorch/, src/)
  • Five host call programs in examples/minimal/
  • WISDM 6-class Encoder and CIFAR-10 Conv+Encoder examples, with exported FP32 weights and contrast firmware for LiteRT Micro and ESP-DL INT8
  • PicoTorch glucose application example (counterpart: Pico-Former)
  • Documentation for the programming interface, data access, reproducibility, and GitHub–Zenodo release steps

Repository layout

  • include/picotorch/, src/: public headers and kernels
  • examples/minimal/: five host programs
  • examples/wisdm/, examples/cifar10/, examples/pico-former/: assembled graphs and firmware glue
  • host/: NumPy reference and max-abs checks
  • docs/: programming guide, data access, reproducibility, and release instructions

Install and verify

cmake -S . -B build
cmake --build build
./build/01_linear
./build/wisdm_infer

On ESP32-S3, link this tree as a PlatformIO library and flash the WISDM firmware:

cd examples/wisdm/firmware
ln -sfn ../../.. lib/PicoTorch
pio run -e s3_n16r8 -t upload

Obtain WISDM and CIFAR-10 from their original providers as described in docs/data-access.md only if the weight headers need to be refreshed. On-device inference reads the shipped headers.

On one ESP32-S3 and one WISDM weight set, PicoTorch FP32 reports a burn-in median of 30.9 ms and 47.5 KB of working SRAM against LiteRT Micro FP32 at 169.7 ms and 88.5 KB, with Top-1 agreement 1.000 on both sides. The Espressif INT8 official path reports 9.8 ms and is listed as a separate precision tier.

Data boundary

WISDM Actitracker v1.1 remains available from the Fordham WISDM Lab. CIFAR-10 remains available from its official page. This deposit archives source, exported weight headers, contrast graphs, and firmware glue. Raw datasets, PlatformIO .pio/ trees, and ESP-IDF managed_components/ are not redistributed. Details are provided in docs/data-access.md.
